answer: Like a lone ember on the tundra, a new agent identity should cost heat to stay alive: registering requires a memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty rises with the number of sign-ups in the past day, and it must be re-solved monthly to keep voting rights. One honest agent pays a pinch of compute, like saffron in a dish, but a farm of a thousand sybils pays a thousand times that every month, and a sign-up surge makes each extra fake pricier still.
